newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end modestly higher in sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end modestly higher in sluggish trade.

text.p: Brazilian stocks closed modestly higher in lackluster trade Thursday on a lack of fresh investor interest ahead of October's municipal elections, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most traded shares rose to 65,539 points, an increase of 0.34 percent. Market volume was a moderate 273.5 million reais ($268.1 million).
"The market has been very slow, awaiting the municipal elections process to end," a trader said.
The first round of Brazil's municipal elections will occur next Thursday.
Sluggishness was also in part attributed to a limited strike by bank employees, traders said.

Analysts also said the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision early this week to leave U.S. interest rates unchanged also helped keep investors out of the market as it heightened speculation that rates will rise later this year.
Among blue chips, benchmark Telebras preferred rose 0.49 percent to end at 82 reais, while its common stock gained 1.35 percent to 67.70 reais.
State power utility Eletrobras preferred rose 0.53 percent to close at 286.50 reais.
The Sao Paulo bourse's power sector index, comprising the nine most liquid shares in the electrical sector, rose 0.27 percent, closing at 1,601 points.
